title: Should Governments or Markets control AI? Dean Ball × Daniel Kokotajlo Anti-Debate

media.diarization: FluidAudio offline = pyannote community-1 CoreML, VBx (diarization.fluidaudio.json)

publishedSynthesis: Third-party verification and auditing of frontier labs is a logical next step both endorse
Establish the preconditions (e.g. enforceability, knowing where the chips are) for an eventual US–China bilateral agreement to slow down or shut down, even if the deal itself is far off

Concentration of power is dangerous whether in government or a dominant lab; neither wants the executive branch to gain unchecked power, and existing checks such as the judiciary should be strengthened
AI alignment is unresolved and urgent, and neither markets nor governments can be blindly trusted to handle it without better verification, auditing and incentives
reference.verifiedAgainst: moderator summary in the recording (~01:23:38–01:24:12) plus Synthesis Media and/or Jasmine Li's notes; the earlier 'transparency as the immediate step' item was not a stated convergence and was dropped
cruxes: At what point do risks from AI outweigh risks from centralised government power?
Do market incentives actually incentivise alignment? (would flip Ball)
Will private governance mechanisms work without regulation? (would flip Kokotajlo)
Timelines: how fast knowledge work is automated
Can third-party auditors gain enough power fast enough?
